newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: BUSH FIRES IN QUEENSLAND AND SOUTH AUSTRALIA
Bush fires are taxing firefighters in Queensland and South Australia.
In Queensland, the problem is searing temperatures and high winds in the south-east and western downs, while in South Australia lightning has sparked most of the fires, mainly in the Flinders Ranges.
At Tara, west of Dalby in Queensland, a fire which broke out overnight could threaten homes.
More than four-thousand volunteer firefighters are on standby in the state with bushfires expected to spread in temperatures forecast to nudge forty degrees and strong winds.
The Emergency Services and police ministers will make an aerial inspection of fire affected areas.

South Australia's Country Fire Service says more than 2,000 fire-fighters have been battling more than 80 fires across the State Aerial surveillance this morning is expected to show the situation has worsened after more lightning overnight, and there are already reports of property damage.
HIGH WINDS HIT SYDNEY
Mopping up operations are underway after strong winds brought down trees and powerlines around Sydney.
The winds struck early this morning. A house in Currajong in the city's north west lost its roof.
At one stage, 7,000 on the North Shore and Central Coast were without power.
But a spokesman for Sydney Electricity says power has been restored to all but a few hundred homes in the city's north.
ROBERT HUGHES CALLS FOR REPUBLIC CONVENTION
Art critic, Robert Hughes, says the Government is making a mockery of the democratic process in the way it's handling the proposed People's Convention on the Republic.
Mr Hughes says it's a farce for the Government, rather than the people, to appoint delegates to the convention.
He told a 2,000 strong rally at Sydney Town Hall last night the Government could stack the convention with monarchists, for the vote outcome it wants.
He called on the Government to keep its promise to hold the People's Convention.
The rally was organised by the Australian Republican Movement.
MINERS UNION SAYS STRIKE WILL CONTINUE
The coal miners union president says New South Wales miners will stay on strike until legislation is changed to restore compensation benefits.
Coal miners went out last Thursday after the Opposition backed amendments to the Workcover Act which cut payouts to injured mineworkers by a quarter.
Miners meet this morning to vote on resolutions which could see them return to work tonight.
The State Government plans to introduce legislation to the Upper House today which will restore miners' benefits.
The union has already rejected a compromise proposed by Opposition leader Peter Collins, allowing employers to make up the shortfall in payouts.
NT GOVERNMENT TO FIGHT ABORIGINAL CLAIM OVER DARWIN
Northern Territory Chief Minister, Shane Stone, has branded an Aboriginal land claim over the city of Darwin, a cheap money grab.
The Larrakia people have announced what is the first comprehensive native title claim over an Australian capital city.
But Mr Stone says the Government will fight the claim.
The Larrakia maintain Darwin makes up their traditional hunting grounds and living areas.
They say the claim, covering undeveloped crown land, would not change the way beaches, parks and nature reserves are used.
They also want to negotiate compensation for land already developed, including the new port still under construction.
TELSTRA DEBATE COULD BEGIN TOMORROW
Debate on the Federal Govenment's partial sale of Telstra Bill has been tentatively set down for tomorrow.
The Coaltion needs the votes of the two independent Senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston to get the bill through because of strong opposition to the bill from the Australian Democrats and Labor.
Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot says she expects the bill will be rejected by Senate on the first vote.
Ms Kernot says she thinks the Government keeps postponing the vote because it's not confident on how the independents will vote.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
